heuristic.applicability: Prefer when phase is the dominant uncertainty: closure timing differs, the skill is invoked after a predecessor at a just-closed or already-lifted state, or the source is already secured and bowl-relative staging is more important than displaced-source acquisition. Requires reliable finger width, container elevation and two-frame co-motion cues.

handoff.entry_conditions: Observed container and bowl poses are finite; gripper may be open near approach or closed with plausible source/TCP co-motion. Prefer closed/already-lifted entries or ambiguous closure timing over a strongly displaced ungrasped source.
handoff.exit_conditions: Auxiliary phase evidence and physical observations agree that fingers are closed, source and TCP co-move, the source is clear, and the bowl-frame stage pose is reached with only a small tilt.
handoff.failure_signatures: Phase prediction disagrees with physical finger/elevation/co-motion evidence, closed fingers without source motion, source drop, early particle escape, or IK failure/limit contact. The phase head is not contact truth.
handoff.overlap_role: The complete [180,360) lift/carry/stage interval is duplicated as action supervision and aligns the bowl-frame output with controlled_pour_and_right, including the small initial tilt.
handoff.successor_readiness: Use observed closure, co-motion and clearance—not the auxiliary class alone—to admit controlled_pour_and_right; nominal readiness is the demonstrated high bowl-relative stage.

heuristic.limitations: The three-class auxiliary target is a causal proxy derived from demonstrated finger width and source elevation, not force/contact truth; it cannot certify a grasp or recover a slip. Bowl-frame absolute targets favor secured carry/staging but do not make pregrasp actions invariant to source-only displacement, which is covered by the source-frame prior. The demonstrations have only successful nominal ordering and one bowl pose, so unseen reordering, large bowl rotations, source displacement, and unreachable bowl locations remain unsupported.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: The auxiliary cross-entropy shares the trainable condition encoder with diffusion and is masked, but inference remains causal and uses no future labels. The agent should prefer this policy for already-grasped or phase-ambiguous entries, cross-check inferred phase against finger and co-motion observations, and use source-frame acquisition when the ungrasped source is displaced. Every bowl-frame target is decoded through shared IK from current joints.
heuristic.rationale: Observed closure timing varies: demo12300 first commands closure at index 148, whereas demo12303 commands closure by 136 and has closed fingers by 140. Their index-180 source heights differ (about 0.029 versus 0.056 m), yet both converge to the bowl-relative high stage around indices 320-360. A registered condition encoder and masked auxiliary head classify causal approach/open, closed-low, and closed-lifted state while the main DDPM predicts bowl-frame Cartesian targets. The auxiliary gradient shapes the same condition features used by the unchanged standard backbone, targeting phase ambiguity without replacing action diffusion.
heuristic.statement: Bowl-frame absolute Cartesian targets with a shared causal phase auxiliary objective for closure/lift ambiguity and robust successor staging.

assignment.subgoal: Approach the container handle at the declared local grasp site, close the fingers, infer a secure grasp from finger closure and container/TCP co-motion, lift the particle-filled source clear of the table, and carry it upright to a high pose above the bowl. Maintain handle contact after closure and avoid disturbing the bowl or spilling particles. Approximate entry: open gripper, source upright on the table. Approximate exit: closed gripper, source near (-0.259,0.224,0.400) m above the bowl with only a small initial tilt.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Compose an encoded bowl-frame target with the same chunk bowl pose and compare FK of IK output to the demonstrated commanded TCP in metres/radians, with unchanged gripper scalar. Robust Gram-Schmidt only projects sampled 6D rotations; encoded labels are exact.

contract.cut_relation: Uses all twelve assigned [0,360) segments and retains the complete [180,360) action-supervised successor overlap. The causal phase auxiliary refines conditioning without changing the cut, future access, success definition, or handoff responsibility.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is an absolute Cartesian TCP target expressed in the destination bowl pose frozen at chunk construction: bowl-frame position xyz in metres, bowl-frame orientation as the first two rotation-matrix columns (6D), and one native gripper scalar. The decoder projects 6D to SO(3), left-composes the frozen bowl pose, and calls panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh measured joints. Slots represent t-1 through t+14; execution uses slots 1 through 8. The gripper scalar retains >=0 open and <0 close semantics. A training-only masked auxiliary classifies causal open/approach, closed-low, or closed-lifted state and does not alter decoding.
contract.parameter_semantics: source_object selects the observed manipulated container used in phase and co-motion features; destination_object selects the observed bowl whose pose is the per-chunk Cartesian action frame. These are semantic references, not phase labels or actuator inputs.
